chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Bat'tat narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, who linked it up to Zurarah ibn Awfi,

he said: 'I entered upon Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them) and he said: O Zurarah! The people in our time are in six groups: lions, wolves, foxes, dogs, pigs, and ewes. As for the lion, they are the kings of the world, each of whom loves to conquer and not be conquered. As for the wolf, they are your merchants; they are criticized when they buy, and praised when they sell. As for the fox, they are those who consume their religion [as a means of livelihood], and what is in their hearts is not what they describe with their tongues. As for the dog, he barks at the people with his tongue, and the people honor him due to the evil of his tongue. As for the pig, they are the effeminate ones and their like, who do not refuse to participate in indecency when invited. As for the ewe, they are the believers whose hair is shaved, whose meat is eaten, and whose bones are broken. So how does the ewe fare among the lion, wolf, fox, dog, and pig?'

key_terms.يَأْكُلُونَ بِأَدْيَانِهِمْ: consume their religion (using faith for worldly gain)

ai.seo_question: What are the six types of people described by Ali ibn al-Hussein in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this famous hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Hussein (Zayn al-Abidin) categorizes society into six archetypes, using animal metaphors to critique the socio-political dynamics of the Umayyad era. While the first five groups represent various forms of power, greed, and hypocrisy, the 'sheep' symbolizes the vulnerable believers who are exploited by the dominant classes, raising the crucial question of how the faithful should navigate this hierarchy. This classification serves as a practical guide for Shia social ethics, distinguishing between those who consume others and those who are consumed.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-44 Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ja’far ibn Bat’tat quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father who linked it up to Zurarah ibn Oa’fi, “I went to Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB) and he said, ‘O Zurarah! The people at these times are in six groups: lions, wolves, foxes, dogs, pigs and ewes. As for the lions, they are the Kings of the world whichever one loves to can conquer and not get defeated. As for the wolves - they are your businessmen. They find faults36 when they want to buy, and they praise when37 they want to sell. And as for the foxes, they are those who use their religion as a means to eat.38 What they describe by their tongues is not in their hearts. And as for the dogs, they are those who growl at the people with their tongues, and the people honor them due to fear of their tongues. And as for the pigs, they are the effeminate ones, and their look-alikes who never refuse to participate in acts of corruption when they are invited. And as for the ewes, they are the believers whose hair is shaved, whose meat is eaten, and whose bones are broken just as when ewes are caught in between lions, wolves, foxes, dogs and pigs.’”
